name: Aloe Flesh
description: The product set among freshly cut aloe leaves laid face to camera, their gel-filled flesh reading genuinely translucent against a low backlight, real mucilage drawing viscous strings between the cut faces. Botanical and clinical at once — the plant's interior, not its silhouette.
lighting: Cool diffused key, low backlight through the flesh
subject: product
prompt: the subject is the hero of the frame and occupies roughly 55 percent of the frame height, tack-sharp and clearly lit and brighter than everything around it, set among freshly cut aloe leaves laid with their severed faces toward camera so the gel-filled flesh reads as genuinely translucent — a clear jelly core banded with visible fibre inside a thick wax-green rind, the serrated margins still stiff and pale at the tips, a fine chalky bloom on the outer skin, real mucilage drawing thin viscous strings between two cut faces and hanging in a slow thick-waisted sag rather than a clean droplet, clear gel pooling and standing under its own surface tension where a leaf has been sliced flat, a fine condensation film across the rind, cool diffused daylight from high camera-left for form plus a second soft backlight raking low through the cut leaves so light travels through the flesh and lights it from inside rather than bouncing off it, cool green and celadon with pale yellow-green at the translucent cores and one cold silver highlight on the subject, the leaves treated as supporting texture cropped tight around the product rather than shown as a whole plant, shallow depth of field with only the product and the nearest cut face crisp, genuine plant cell structure and fibre visible inside the gel, real fluid viscosity in the strings, no soil, no pot, no whole aloe rosette, no gradient studio backdrop, no warm light, no second product, immaculate close-range commercial clarity
